pmid:30735751.authors: Chartoumpekis DV, Ziros PG, Chen JG, et al.
pmid:30735751.title: Broccoli sprout beverage is safe for thyroid hormonal and autoimmune status: Results of a 12-week randomized trial.
pmid:30735751.finding: 84 days of a sulforaphane/glucoraphanin beverage did not change TSH, free T4, thyroglobulin or thyroid autoimmunity.

pmid:11525594.authors: Conaway CC, Getahun SM, Liebes LL, et al.
pmid:11525594.title: Disposition of glucosinolates and sulforaphane in humans after ingestion of steamed and fresh broccoli.
pmid:11525594.finding: After 200 g broccoli, 32% of isothiocyanates were excreted from fresh vs 10% from steamed broccoli (~3x difference).

pmid:18950181.authors: Vermeulen M, Klöpping-Ketelaars IW, van den Berg R, et al.
pmid:18950181.title: Bioavailability and kinetics of sulforaphane in humans after consumption of cooked versus raw broccoli.
pmid:18950181.finding: Sulforaphane bioavailability was 37% from raw vs 3.4% from cooked broccoli; peak at 1.6 vs 6 h; half-life ~2.5 h.

pmid:15184012.authors: Matusheski NV, Juvik JA, Jeffery EH
pmid:15184012.title: Heating decreases epithiospecifier protein activity and increases sulforaphane formation in broccoli.
pmid:15184012.finding: Heating broccoli to 60 °C increased sulforaphane and decreased inactive nitrile formation; 70 °C and above decreased both in florets.

pmid:29266773.authors: Sivapalan T, Melchini A, Saha S, et al.
pmid:29266773.title: Bioavailability of Glucoraphanin and Sulforaphane from High-Glucoraphanin Broccoli.
pmid:29266773.finding: Soups (myrosinase denatured) from high-glucoraphanin broccoli gave 3-5x higher circulating sulforaphane; excretion was 2-15% of glucoraphanin consumed.

pmid:29806738.authors: Okunade O, Niranjan K, Ghawi SK, et al.
pmid:29806738.title: Supplementation of the Diet by Exogenous Myrosinase via Mustard Seeds to Increase the Bioavailability of Sulforaphane in Healthy Human Subjects after the Consumption of Cooked Broccoli.
pmid:29806738.finding: Adding 1 g brown mustard powder to 200 g cooked broccoli raised urinary sulforaphane-NAC from 9.8 to 44.7 µmol/g creatinine.

pmid:26881038.authors: Houghton CA, Fassett RG, Coombes JS
pmid:26881038.title: Sulforaphane and Other Nutrigenomic Nrf2 Activators: Can the Clinician's Expectation Be Matched by the Reality?
pmid:26881038.finding: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2 more potently and is more bioavailable than curcumin, silymarin or resveratrol.

pmid:26604653.authors: Kikuchi M, Ushida Y, Shiozawa H, et al.
pmid:26604653.title: Sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extract improves hepatic abnormalities in male subjects.
pmid:26604653.finding: Glucoraphanin capsules for 2 months lowered ALT, gamma-GTP and urinary 8-OHdG vs placebo.

pmid:31136659.authors: Curtis PJ, van der Velpen V, Berends L, et al.
pmid:31136659.title: Blueberries improve biomarkers of cardiometabolic function in participants with metabolic syndrome-results from a 6-month, double-blind, randomized controlled trial.
pmid:31136659.finding: 1 cup (150 g)/day blueberries improved FMD (+1.45%) and arterial stiffness over 6 months; 1/2 cup had no effect; insulin resistance and plasma thiols unchanged.

pmid:24004888.authors: Rodriguez-Mateos A, Rendeiro C, Bergillos-Meca T, et al.
pmid:24004888.title: Intake and time dependence of blueberry flavonoid-induced improvements in vascular function: a randomized, controlled, double-blind, crossover intervention study with mechanistic insights into biological activity.
pmid:24004888.finding: FMD rose at 1-2 and 6 h after blueberry; dose-dependent up to 766 mg polyphenols then plateaued; linked to metabolites and lower neutrophil NADPH oxidase.

pmid:26024297.authors: Stull AJ, Cash KC, Champagne CM, et al.
pmid:26024297.title: Blueberries improve endothelial function, but not blood pressure, in adults with metabolic syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
pmid:26024297.finding: Blueberry smoothies twice daily for 6 weeks improved endothelial function (RHI) but not blood pressure or insulin sensitivity.

pmid:29019365.authors: Nair AR, Mariappan N, Stull AJ, et al.
pmid:29019365.title: Blueberry supplementation attenuates oxidative stress within monocytes and modulates immune cell levels in adults with metabolic syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:29019365.finding: 22.5 g freeze-dried blueberry twice daily for 6 weeks lowered superoxide and total ROS in whole blood and monocytes.

pmid:20660279.authors: Basu A, Du M, Leyva MJ, et al.
pmid:20660279.title: Blueberries decrease cardiovascular risk factors in obese men and women with metabolic syndrome.
pmid:20660279.finding: 50 g freeze-dried blueberries (~350 g fresh) daily for 8 weeks reduced blood pressure and oxidized LDL (-28%) and MDA/HNE more than control.

pmid:22733001.authors: Riso P, Klimis-Zacas D, Del Bo' C, et al.
pmid:22733001.title: Effect of a wild blueberry (Vaccinium angustifolium) drink intervention on markers of oxidative stress, inflammation and endothelial function in humans with cardiovascular risk factors.
pmid:22733001.finding: Wild blueberry drink (375 mg anthocyanins) for 6 weeks reduced oxidized DNA bases and H2O2-induced DNA damage; no effect on endothelial markers.

pmid:25578927.authors: Johnson SA, Figueroa A, Navaei N, et al.
pmid:25578927.title: Daily blueberry consumption improves blood pressure and arterial stiffness in postmenopausal women with pre- and stage 1-hypertension: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
pmid:25578927.finding: 22 g/day freeze-dried blueberry for 8 weeks lowered blood pressure and arterial stiffness and raised nitric oxide.

pmid:36847333.authors: Woolf EK, Terwoord JD, Litwin NS, et al.
pmid:36847333.title: Daily blueberry consumption for 12 weeks improves endothelial function in postmenopausal women with above-normal blood pressure through reductions in oxidative stress: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:36847333.finding: 22 g/day freeze-dried blueberry for 12 weeks improved FMD, and the smaller response to ascorbate infusion implied the gain came from reduced oxidative stress.

pmid:36150681.authors: Martini D, Marino M, Venturi S, et al.
pmid:36150681.title: Blueberries and their bioactives in the modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation and cardio/vascular function markers: a systematic review of human intervention studies.
pmid:36150681.finding: Blueberries most consistently improve vascular function; results on oxidative stress, inflammation and cardiometabolic markers conflict.

pmid:28825651.authors: Fairlie-Jones L, Davison K, Fromentin E, et al.
pmid:28825651.title: The Effect of Anthocyanin-Rich Foods or Extracts on Vascular Function in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
pmid:28825651.finding: Anthocyanin foods/extracts improved FMD acutely and chronically (chronic SMD 0.84) with high heterogeneity.

pmid:23604435.authors: Czank C, Cassidy A, Zhang Q, et al.
pmid:23604435.title: Human metabolism and elimination of the anthocyanin, cyanidin-3-glucoside: a (13)C-tracer study.
pmid:23604435.finding: Relative bioavailability of labelled cyanidin-3-glucoside including metabolites was ~12%; metabolites (phenolic, hippuric acids) circulated for up to 48 h.

pmid:27006201.authors: Huang H, Chen G, Liao D, et al.
pmid:27006201.title: Effects of Berries Consumption on Cardiovascular Risk Factors: A Meta-analysis with Trial Sequential Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:27006201.finding: Berries lowered LDL (-0.21 mmol/L), systolic BP (-2.7 mmHg), fasting glucose, HbA1c and TNF-alpha.

pmid:23319811.authors: Cassidy A, Mukamal KJ, Liu L, et al.
pmid:23319811.title: High anthocyanin intake is associated with a reduced risk of myocardial infarction in young and middle-aged women.
pmid:23319811.finding: Highest vs lowest anthocyanin quintile: MI HR 0.68; >3 servings/week of blueberries + strawberries HR 0.66 (CI crossed 1).

pmid:30096878.authors: Solverson PM, Rumpler WV, Leger JL, et al.
pmid:30096878.title: Blackberry Feeding Increases Fat Oxidation and Improves Insulin Sensitivity in Overweight and Obese Males.
pmid:30096878.finding: 600 g/day blackberries for 7 days on a high-fat diet lowered respiratory quotient and insulin AUC and improved HOMA-IR.

pmid:10962130.authors: Noda Y, Kneyuki T, Igarashi K, et al.
pmid:10962130.title: Antioxidant activity of nasunin, an anthocyanin in eggplant peels.
pmid:10962130.finding: Nasunin scavenged superoxide, inhibited hydroxyl radical generation by chelating iron, and protected rat brain homogenate from lipid peroxidation in vitro.

pmid:12744682.title: Distribution of hydroxycinnamic acid conjugates in fruit of commercial eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) cultivars.
pmid:12744682.finding: Chlorogenic acid is the predominant eggplant phenolic, with large differences among cultivars and fruit segments.

pmid:29195964.authors: Kaushik P, Gramazio P, Vilanova S, et al.
pmid:29195964.title: Phenolics content, fruit flesh colour and browning in cultivated eggplant, wild relatives and interspecific hybrids and implications for fruit quality breeding.
pmid:29195964.finding: Chlorogenic acid made up >65% of phenolic acids in cultivated eggplant; wild relatives had more phenolics.

pmid:31744060.authors: Nishimura M, Suzuki M, Takahashi R, et al.
pmid:31744060.title: Daily Ingestion of Eggplant Powder Improves Blood Pressure and Psychological State in Stressed Individuals: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Study.
pmid:31744060.finding: 1.2 g/day eggplant powder for 12 weeks lowered blood pressure, attributed to acetylcholine (choline esters), not antioxidants.

pmid:27483219.authors: Martini D, Del Bo' C, Tassotti M, et al.
pmid:27483219.title: Coffee Consumption and Oxidative Stress: A Review of Human Intervention Studies.
pmid:27483219.finding: Coffee can raise glutathione and protect against DNA damage, especially with regular intake; effects on antioxidant capacity, enzymes and lipid/protein damage are unclear.

pmid:20589860.authors: Hoelzl C, Knasmüller S, Wagner KH, et al.
pmid:20589860.title: Instant coffee with high chlorogenic acid levels protects humans against oxidative damage of macromolecules.
pmid:20589860.finding: 800 mL/day high-chlorogenic-acid coffee for 5 days lowered urinary 8-iso-PGF2alpha by 15% and 3-nitrotyrosine by 16%.

pmid:24740588.authors: Bakuradze T, Lang R, Hofmann T, et al.
pmid:24740588.title: Consumption of a dark roast coffee decreases the level of spontaneous DNA strand breaks: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:24740588.finding: 750 mL/day coffee for 4 weeks produced a 27% difference in spontaneous DNA strand breaks vs water.

pmid:26632023.authors: Bakuradze T, Lang R, Hofmann T, et al.
pmid:26632023.title: Coffee consumption rapidly reduces background DNA strand breaks in healthy humans: Results of a short-term repeated uptake intervention study.
pmid:26632023.finding: DNA strand breaks fell within 2 h of the first cup and by about one-third after 800 mL over 8 h.

pmid:29160894.authors: Clifford MN, Jaganath IB, Ludwig IA, et al.
pmid:29160894.title: Chlorogenic acids and the acyl-quinic acids: discovery, biosynthesis, bioavailability and bioactivity.
pmid:29160894.finding: Coffee is the major dietary source of chlorogenic (acyl-quinic) acids worldwide; much is metabolised by colonic microbiota.

pmid:29167102.authors: Poole R, Kennedy OJ, Roderick P, et al.
pmid:29167102.title: Coffee consumption and health: umbrella review of meta-analyses of multiple health outcomes.
pmid:29167102.finding: Largest risk reductions at 3-4 cups/day (all-cause mortality RR 0.83); harms in pregnancy.

pmid:26572796.authors: Ding M, Satija A, Bhupathiraju SN, et al.
pmid:26572796.title: Association of Coffee Consumption With Total and Cause-Specific Mortality in 3 Large Prospective Cohorts.
pmid:26572796.finding: Caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee were both inversely associated with mortality in never smokers.

pmid:9240930.title: The cholesterol-raising factor from coffee beans.
pmid:9240930.finding: Cafestol and kahweol raise LDL cholesterol; paper filters retain them, so filtered coffee does not raise cholesterol while boiled, cafetiere and Turkish coffee do.

pmid:9234024.authors: Urgert R, Weusten-van der Wouw MP, Hovenier R, et al.
pmid:9234024.title: Diterpenes from coffee beans decrease serum levels of lipoprotein(a) in humans: results from four randomised controlled trials.
pmid:9234024.finding: 10 mg/day cafestol corresponds to two to three cups of cafetiere coffee.

pmid:20167460.authors: Medina-Remón A, Zamora-Ros R, Rotchés-Ribalta M, et al.
pmid:20167460.title: Total polyphenol excretion and blood pressure in subjects at high cardiovascular risk.
pmid:20167460.finding: Fruit and vegetables, then coffee, then wine contributed most to urinary polyphenols; higher excretion associated with lower blood pressure.

pmid:14519830.authors: Hakim IA, Harris RB, Brown S, et al.
pmid:14519830.title: Effect of increased tea consumption on oxidative DNA damage among smokers: a randomized controlled study.
pmid:14519830.finding: 4 cups/day decaffeinated green tea for 4 months lowered urinary 8-OHdG by 31%; black tea had no effect.

pmid:20595643.authors: Basu A, Sanchez K, Leyva MJ, et al.
pmid:20595643.title: Green tea supplementation affects body weight, lipids, and lipid peroxidation in obese subjects with metabolic syndrome.
pmid:20595643.finding: 4 cups/day green tea for 8 weeks lowered plasma MDA and HNE vs control.

pmid:12376503.authors: Lee MJ, Maliakal P, Chen L, et al.
pmid:12376503.title: Pharmacokinetics of tea catechins after ingestion of green tea and (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate by humans: formation of different metabolites and individual variability.
pmid:12376503.finding: EGCG peaked in plasma at ~1.5 h with a 3.4 h half-life and large variability; valerolactone ring-fission metabolites peaked at 8-15 h.

pmid:32625874.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS), Younes M, Aggett P, et al.
pmid:32625874.title: Scientific opinion on the safety of green tea catechins.
pmid:32625874.finding: Brewed green tea is generally safe (90-300 mg EGCG/day typical); supplement intakes >= 800 mg EGCG/day significantly raise serum transaminases in trials.

pmid:25975988.authors: Mazzanti G, Di Sotto A, Vitalone A
pmid:25975988.title: Hepatotoxicity of green tea: an update.
pmid:25975988.finding: Green-tea supplement liver injury cases were mostly hepatocellular in women; multi-ingredient products caused more severe injury with shorter latency.

pmid:42016115.authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
pmid:42016115.title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of a health claim related to cocoa flavanols and maintenance of normal endothelium-dependent vasodilation pursuant to Article 13(5) of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006.
pmid:42016115.finding: Cause-and-effect established; 200 mg cocoa flavanols/day (2.5 g high-flavanol cocoa powder or 10 g high-flavanol dark chocolate) needed.

pmid:22301923.authors: Hooper L, Kay C, Abdelhamid A, et al.
pmid:22301923.title: Effects of chocolate, cocoa, and flavan-3-ols on cardiovascular health: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
pmid:22301923.finding: Cocoa improved FMD (chronic +1.34%, acute +3.19%) regardless of dose, insulin resistance and diastolic BP; >50 mg epicatechin/day gave larger BP effects.

pmid:26348767.authors: Sansone R, Rodriguez-Mateos A, Heuel J, et al.
pmid:26348767.title: Cocoa flavanol intake improves endothelial function and Framingham Risk Score in healthy men and women: a randomised, controlled, double-masked trial: the Flaviola Health Study.
pmid:26348767.finding: 450 mg cocoa flavanols twice daily for 1 month raised FMD by 1.2% and lowered BP, LDL and pulse wave velocity; FMD plateaued after ~2 weeks.

pmid:35294962.authors: Sesso HD, Manson JE, Aragaki AK, et al.
pmid:35294962.title: Effect of cocoa flavanol supplementation for the prevention of cardiovascular disease events: the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) randomized clinical trial.
pmid:35294962.finding: 500 mg/day cocoa flavanols for 3.6 years: total CVD events HR 0.90 (NS); CVD death HR 0.73 (secondary).

pmid:16954359.authors: Covas MI, Nyyssönen K, Poulsen HE, et al.
pmid:16954359.title: The effect of polyphenols in olive oil on heart disease risk factors: a randomized trial.
pmid:16954359.finding: 25 mL/day olive oil for 3 weeks: HDL rose and oxidized LDL and oxidative stress markers fell linearly with phenolic content (2.7, 164, 366 mg/kg).

pmid:42078706.authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
pmid:42078706.title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of health claims related to polyphenols in olive and protection of LDL particles from oxidative damage (ID 1333, 1638, 1639, 1696, 2865), maintenance of normal blood HDL cholesterol concentrations (ID 1639), maintenance of normal blood pressure (ID 3781), "anti-inflammatory properties" (ID 1882), "contributes to the upper respiratory tract health" (ID 3468), "can help to maintain a normal function of gastrointestinal tract" (3779), and "contributes to body defences against external agents" (ID 3467) pursuant to Article 13(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006.
pmid:42078706.finding: EFSA opinion underpinning the authorised claim that olive oil polyphenols contribute to protecting blood lipids (LDL) from oxidative stress.

pmid:30884804.authors: Tsimidou MZ, Sotiroglou M, Mastralexi A, et al.
pmid:30884804.title: In House Validated UHPLC Protocol for the Determination of the Total Hydroxytyrosol and Tyrosol Content in Virgin Olive Oil Fit for the Purpose of the Health Claim Introduced by the EC Regulation 432/2012 for "Olive Oil Polyphenols".
pmid:30884804.finding: The EC 432/2012 claim requires at least 5 mg of olive oil polyphenols (hydroxytyrosol and derivatives) per 20 g of oil; measurement methods are still debated.

pmid:28371298.authors: Hernáez Á, Castañer O, Goday A, et al.
pmid:28371298.title: The Mediterranean Diet decreases LDL atherogenicity in high cardiovascular risk individuals: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:28371298.finding: MedDiet + virgin olive oil for 1 year raised LDL resistance to oxidation (+6.5%) and lowered LDL oxidative modifications (-36%) vs low-fat diet; the nut arm did not.

pmid:29897866.authors: Estruch R, Ros E, Salas-Salvadó J, et al.
pmid:29897866.title: Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet Supplemented with Extra-Virgin Olive Oil or Nuts.
pmid:29897866.finding: Major CVD events HR 0.69 (EVOO) and 0.72 (nuts) vs reduced-fat diet over 4.8 years, robust to randomisation-protocol deviations.

pmid:22999065.authors: Mitjavila MT, Fandos M, Salas-Salvadó J, et al.
pmid:22999065.title: The Mediterranean diet improves the systemic lipid and DNA oxidative damage in metabolic syndrome individuals. A randomized, controlled, trial.
pmid:22999065.finding: After 1 year, urinary 8-oxo-dG fell more in both MedDiet arms (P<0.001) and F2-isoprostanes showed a borderline larger fall vs low-fat control.

pmid:15037535.authors: Ros E, Núñez I, Pérez-Heras A, et al.
pmid:15037535.title: A walnut diet improves endothelial function in hypercholesterolemic subjects: a randomized crossover trial.
pmid:15037535.finding: Walnuts replacing ~32% of MUFA energy for 4 weeks improved endothelium-dependent vasodilation and lowered LDL; oxidation biomarkers unchanged.

pmid:29931130.authors: Guasch-Ferré M, Li J, Hu FB, et al.
pmid:29931130.title: Effects of walnut consumption on blood lipids and other cardiovascular risk factors: an updated meta-analysis and systematic review of controlled trials.
pmid:29931130.finding: Walnut diets lowered total cholesterol (-7.0 mg/dL), LDL (-5.5 mg/dL), triglycerides and apoB without weight gain.

pmid:19703258.authors: López-Uriarte P, Bulló M, Casas-Agustench P, et al.
pmid:19703258.title: Nuts and oxidation: a systematic review.
pmid:19703258.finding: Reviews in vitro, animal and human studies of nut intake on oxidation; nuts are fat-rich but their skins carry antioxidants.

pmid:9209178.authors: Gärtner C, Stahl W, Sies H
pmid:9209178.title: Lycopene is more bioavailable from tomato paste than from fresh tomatoes.
pmid:9209178.finding: With 15 g oil, tomato paste gave 2.5x higher peak and 3.8x higher AUC lycopene than fresh tomatoes.

pmid:15735074.authors: Unlu NZ, Bohn T, Clinton SK, et al.
pmid:15735074.title: Carotenoid absorption from salad and salsa by humans is enhanced by the addition of avocado or avocado oil.
pmid:15735074.finding: Adding 150 g avocado or 24 g avocado oil raised carotenoid absorption 2.6-15-fold.

pmid:15277161.authors: Brown MJ, Ferruzzi MG, Nguyen ML, et al.
pmid:15277161.title: Carotenoid bioavailability is higher from salads ingested with full-fat than with fat-reduced salad dressings as measured with electrochemical detection.
pmid:15277161.finding: Essentially no carotenoid absorption with fat-free dressing; more with 6 g and most with 28 g oil.

pmid:22331646.authors: Burton-Freeman B, Talbot J, Park E, et al.
pmid:22331646.title: Protective activity of processed tomato products on postprandial oxidation and inflammation: a clinical trial in healthy weight men and women.
pmid:22331646.finding: Processed tomato with a high-fat meal attenuated postprandial LDL oxidation and IL-6 rise.

pmid:28129549.authors: Cheng HM, Koutsidis G, Lodge JK, et al.
pmid:28129549.title: Tomato and lycopene supplementation and cardiovascular risk factors: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:28129549.finding: Tomato interventions lowered LDL (-0.22 mmol/L) and IL-6 and improved FMD (+2.53%); lycopene supplements lowered systolic BP; oxidized LDL not significantly changed.

pmid:11588897.authors: Collins BH, Horská A, Hotten PM, et al.
pmid:11588897.title: Kiwifruit protects against oxidative DNA damage in human cells and in vitro.
pmid:11588897.finding: A kiwifruit juice drink increased lymphocyte resistance to H2O2-induced DNA damage ex vivo, not fully explained by vitamin C; no effect on endogenous damage.

pmid:17999464.authors: Anand P, Kunnumakkara AB, Newman RA, et al.
pmid:17999464.title: Bioavailability of curcumin: problems and promises.
pmid:17999464.finding: Curcumin is safe up to 12 g/day but poorly bioavailable due to poor absorption, rapid metabolism and elimination.

pmid:9619120.authors: Shoba G, Joy D, Joseph T, et al.
pmid:9619120.title: Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers.
pmid:9619120.finding: 2 g curcumin alone gave undetectable or very low serum levels; with 20 mg piperine bioavailability rose 2000%.

pmid:15158307.authors: Aviram M, Rosenblat M, Gaitini D, et al.
pmid:15158307.title: Pomegranate juice consumption for 3 years by patients with carotid artery stenosis reduces common carotid intima-media thickness, blood pressure and LDL oxidation.
pmid:15158307.finding: Pomegranate juice reduced LDL oxidation and carotid IMT in a tiny, non-randomised study.

pmid:19766760.authors: Davidson MH, Maki KC, Dicklin MR, et al.
pmid:19766760.title: Effects of consumption of pomegranate juice on carotid intima-media thickness in men and women at moderate risk for coronary heart disease.
pmid:19766760.finding: 240 mL/day pomegranate juice for up to 18 months had no effect on overall carotid IMT progression.

pmid:26857863.authors: Sahebkar A, Simental-Mendía LE, Giorgini P, et al.
pmid:26857863.title: Lipid profile changes after pomegranate consumption: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:26857863.finding: Pomegranate had no significant effect on plasma lipids.

pmid:33484037.authors: Askari M, Mozaffari H, Darooghegi Mofrad M, et al.
pmid:33484037.title: Effects of garlic supplementation on oxidative stress and antioxidative capacity biomarkers: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:33484037.finding: Garlic (80-4000 mg/day) raised TAC and SOD and lowered MDA, with very large heterogeneous effect sizes.

pmid:26764326.title: Garlic Lowers Blood Pressure in Hypertensive Individuals, Regulates Serum Cholesterol, and Stimulates Immunity: An Updated Meta-analysis and Review.
pmid:26764326.finding: Garlic lowered BP by 5.1/2.5 mmHg overall and 8.7/6.1 mmHg in hypertensives.

pmid:15333514.authors: Walle T, Hsieh F, DeLegge MH, et al.
pmid:15333514.title: High absorption but very low bioavailability of oral resveratrol in humans.
pmid:15333514.finding: A 25 mg oral dose was >=70% absorbed but only trace unchanged resveratrol (<5 ng/mL) appeared in plasma due to rapid sulfation.

pmid:24819981.authors: Semba RD, Ferrucci L, Bartali B, et al.
pmid:24819981.title: Resveratrol levels and all-cause mortality in older community-dwelling adults.
pmid:24819981.finding: Urinary resveratrol metabolites from diet did not predict mortality, inflammation, CVD or cancer over 9 years.

pmid:32114706.authors: Abdelhamid AS, Brown TJ, Brainard JS, et al.
pmid:32114706.title: Omega-3 fatty acids for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease.
pmid:32114706.finding: Long-chain omega-3 had little effect on mortality, slightly reduced CHD events (RR 0.91) and lowered triglycerides ~15%.

pmid:10966889.authors: Higdon JV, Liu J, Du SH, et al.
pmid:10966889.title: Supplementation of postmenopausal women with fish oil rich in eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid is not associated with greater in vivo lipid peroxidation compared with oils rich in oleate and linoleate as assessed by plasma malondialdehyde and F(2)-isoprostanes.
pmid:10966889.finding: Fish oil (2.0 g EPA + 1.4 g DHA/day) did not raise F2-isoprostanes or MDA vs sunflower or safflower oil, though TBARS was higher.

pmid:17854006.title: Dietary advanced lipid oxidation endproducts are risk factors to human health.
pmid:17854006.finding: Oxidized dietary fats yield absorbed cytotoxic lipid oxidation end-products; humans excrete more MDA after eating them; dietary antioxidants in the meal may limit this.

pmid:18540628.authors: Gorelik S, Ligumsky M, Kohen R, et al.
pmid:18540628.title: The stomach as a "bioreactor": when red meat meets red wine.
pmid:18540628.finding: In rats, red meat raised stomach lipid hydroperoxides and plasma MDA (+50%); adding red-wine polyphenols prevented the rise.

pmid:24632108.authors: Ng CY, Leong XF, Masbah N, et al.
pmid:24632108.title: Heated vegetable oils and cardiovascular disease risk factors.
pmid:24632108.finding: Repeatedly heated oils generate lipid oxidation products that raise blood pressure, cholesterol and vascular inflammation, mainly in animal models.

pmid:27468708.authors: Vlassara H, Cai W, Tripp E, et al.
pmid:27468708.title: Oral AGE restriction ameliorates insulin resistance in obese individuals with the metabolic syndrome: a randomised controlled trial.
pmid:27468708.finding: A 1-year low-AGE diet lowered HOMA-IR from 3.1 to 1.9 and reduced AGEs, oxidative stress and inflammation; the regular diet worsened them.

pmid:17490958.authors: Negrean M, Stirban A, Stratmann B, et al.
pmid:17490958.title: Effects of low- and high-advanced glycation endproduct meals on macro- and microvascular endothelial function and oxidative stress in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
pmid:17490958.finding: An identical meal cooked to be high-AGE cut FMD by 36% vs 21% for the low-AGE version and raised oxidative stress markers.

pmid:26938557.authors: Clarke RE, Dordevic AL, Tan SM, et al.
pmid:26938557.title: Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Risk Factors for Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
pmid:26938557.finding: High-AGE diets increased TNF-alpha and circulating AGEs, and 8-isoprostanes in healthy adults; evidence quality limited.

pmid:10946914.authors: Mohanty P, Hamouda W, Garg R, et al.
pmid:10946914.title: Glucose challenge stimulates reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation by leucocytes.
pmid:10946914.finding: 75 g glucose raised leukocyte ROS generation to ~240% of baseline at 2 h, increased p47phox and lowered alpha-tocopherol.

pmid:11916766.authors: Mohanty P, Ghanim H, Hamouda W, et al.
pmid:11916766.title: Both lipid and protein intakes stimulate increased generation of reactive oxygen species by polymorphonuclear leukocytes and mononuclear cells.
pmid:11916766.finding: Cream raised leukocyte ROS for 3 h and lipid peroxidation; casein raised ROS for 1 h.

pmid:18206731.authors: O'Keefe JH, Gheewala NM, O'Keefe JO
pmid:18206731.title: Dietary strategies for improving post-prandial glucose, lipids, inflammation, and cardiovascular health.
pmid:18206731.finding: Post-meal glucose and triglyceride spikes induce oxidant stress proportional to their size; minimally processed high-fiber plant foods blunt them.

pmid:26355033.authors: Boden G, Homko C, Barrero CA, et al.
pmid:26355033.title: Excessive caloric intake acutely causes oxidative stress, GLUT4 carbonylation, and insulin resistance in healthy men.
pmid:26355033.finding: ~6000 kcal/day for 1 week caused 3.5 kg gain and systemic and adipose oxidative stress and insulin resistance within 2-3 days.

pmid:22586466.authors: Samocha-Bonet D, Campbell LV, Mori TA, et al.
pmid:22586466.title: Overfeeding reduces insulin sensitivity and increases oxidative stress, without altering markers of mitochondrial content and function in humans.
pmid:22586466.finding: +1040 kcal/day for 28 days raised urinary F2-isoprostanes and muscle protein carbonyls and reduced insulin sensitivity.

pmid:21209396.authors: Bastide NM, Pierre FH, Corpet DE
pmid:21209396.title: Heme iron from meat and risk of colorectal cancer: a meta-analysis and a review of the mechanisms involved.
pmid:21209396.finding: Highest vs lowest heme intake: colon cancer RR 1.18; heme catalyses N-nitrosation and lipoperoxidation to cytotoxic aldehydes.

pmid:26514947.authors: Bouvard V, Loomis D, Guyton KZ, et al.
pmid:26514947.title: Carcinogenicity of consumption of red and processed meat.
pmid:26514947.finding: IARC classified processed meat as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) and red meat as probably carcinogenic (Group 2A).

pmid:12421881.authors: Bingham SA, Hughes R, Cross AJ
pmid:12421881.title: Effect of white versus red meat on endogenous N-nitrosation in the human colon and further evidence of a dose response.
pmid:12421881.finding: Fecal N-nitroso compounds rose linearly with red meat from 0 to 420 g/day; white meat had no effect; fiber did not reduce them.

pmid:15199546.title: Meat-related mutagens/carcinogens in the etiology of colorectal cancer.
pmid:15199546.finding: High-temperature cooking forms HCAs and PAHs; endogenous N-nitroso exposure is dose-dependent on red meat.

pmid:20335545.authors: Li Z, Henning SM, Zhang Y, et al.
pmid:20335545.title: Antioxidant-rich spice added to hamburger meat during cooking results in reduced meat, plasma, and urine malondialdehyde concentrations.
pmid:20335545.finding: Spice blend cut burger MDA by 71%, prevented the plasma MDA rise and lowered urinary MDA by 49%.

pmid:19241593.authors: Smith JS, Ameri F, Gadgil P
pmid:19241593.title: Effect of marinades on the formation of heterocyclic amines in grilled beef steaks.
pmid:19241593.finding: Herb/spice marinades cut total HCAs in steaks grilled at 204 °C by 57-88%.

pmid:21697300.authors: Skulas-Ray AC, Kris-Etherton PM, Teeter DL, et al.
pmid:21697300.title: A high antioxidant spice blend attenuates postprandial insulin and triglyceride responses and increases some plasma measures of antioxidant activity in healthy, overweight men.
pmid:21697300.finding: 14 g spice blend in a meal reduced postprandial insulin (21%) and triglycerides (31%) and raised plasma FRAP.

pmid:16611951.authors: Mozaffarian D, Katan MB, Ascherio A, et al.
pmid:16611951.title: Trans fatty acids and cardiovascular disease.
pmid:16611951.finding: Industrial trans fats adversely affect lipoproteins, inflammation and endothelial function and are strongly linked to coronary heart disease.

pmid:9989688.authors: Lund EK, Wharf SG, Fairweather-Tait SJ, et al.
pmid:9989688.title: Oral ferrous sulfate supplements increase the free radical-generating capacity of feces from healthy volunteers.
pmid:9989688.finding: 19 mg Fe/day for 2 weeks raised weakly bound fecal iron from 60 to 300 µmol/L and fecal free-radical production ~40%.

pmid:10491416.authors: Meagher EA, Barry OP, Burke A, et al.
pmid:10491416.title: Alcohol-induced generation of lipid peroxidation products in humans.
pmid:10491416.finding: Acute alcohol raised urinary isoprostanes in a time- and dose-dependent way tracking blood alcohol; levels were high in alcoholic liver disease.

pmid:29424490.authors: Il'yasova D, Fontana L, Bhapkar M, et al.
pmid:29424490.title: Effects of 2 years of caloric restriction on oxidative status assessed by urinary F2-isoprostanes: The CALERIE 2 randomized clinical trial.
pmid:29424490.finding: Prescribed 25% CR lowered 2,3-dinor-iPF2alpha-III by 17%/13% and iPF2alpha-III by 20%/27% at 12/24 months vs ad libitum.

pmid:16595757.authors: Heilbronn LK, de Jonge L, Frisard MI, et al.
pmid:16595757.title: Effect of 6-month calorie restriction on biomarkers of longevity, metabolic adaptation, and oxidative stress in overweight individuals: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:16595757.finding: 6 months of CR lowered fasting insulin and DNA damage; protein carbonyls unchanged.

pmid:10590217.authors: Thompson HJ, Heimendinger J, Haegele A, et al.
pmid:10590217.title: Effect of increased vegetable and fruit consumption on markers of oxidative cellular damage.
pmid:10590217.finding: Raising produce from 5.8 to 12 servings/day for 14 days lowered lymphocyte and urinary 8-OHdG and urinary 8-isoprostane (uncontrolled).

pmid:14578137.authors: Møller P, Vogel U, Pedersen A, et al.
pmid:14578137.title: No effect of 600 grams fruit and vegetables per day on oxidative DNA damage and repair in healthy nonsmokers.
pmid:14578137.finding: 600 g/day fruit and vegetables or matched vitamins for 24 days did not change oxidative DNA damage or repair.

pmid:12623938.authors: Lopes HF, Martin KL, Nashar K, et al.
pmid:12623938.title: DASH diet lowers blood pressure and lipid-induced oxidative stress in obesity.
pmid:12623938.finding: DASH lowered BP ~8/7 mmHg in obese hypertensives, raised FRAP and prevented the F2-isoprostane rise during lipid infusion.

pmid:29754952.authors: Sutton EF, Beyl R, Early KS, et al.
pmid:29754952.title: Early Time-Restricted Feeding Improves Insulin Sensitivity, Blood Pressure, and Oxidative Stress Even without Weight Loss in Men with Prediabetes.
pmid:29754952.finding: 5 weeks of 6-h early feeding lowered plasma 8-isoprostane by ~14% (p=0.05) vs 12-h feeding without weight loss.

pmid:17291990.authors: Johnson JB, Summer W, Cutler RG, et al.
pmid:17291990.title: Alternate day calorie restriction improves clinical findings and reduces markers of oxidative stress and inflammation in overweight adults with moderate asthma.
pmid:17291990.finding: 8 weeks of alternate-day CR (8% weight loss) reduced 8-isoprostane, nitrotyrosine, protein carbonyls and HNE adducts (uncontrolled).

pmid:31881139.title: Effects of Intermittent Fasting on Health, Aging, and Disease.
pmid:31881139.finding: Reviews metabolic switching and adaptive stress responses (including antioxidant defences) proposed to underlie fasting benefits.

pmid:28338764.authors: Aune D, Giovannucci E, Boffetta P, et al.
pmid:28338764.title: Fruit and vegetable intake and the risk of cardiovascular disease, total cancer and all-cause mortality-a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies.
pmid:28338764.finding: Per 200 g/day: all-cause mortality RR 0.90; reductions up to 800 g/day; strongest for citrus, apples/pears, green leafy and cruciferous vegetables.

pmid:27301975.authors: Aune D, Keum N, Giovannucci E, et al.
pmid:27301975.title: Whole grain consumption and risk of cardiovascular disease, cancer, and all cause and cause specific mortality: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies.
pmid:27301975.finding: Per 90 g/day whole grain: CHD RR 0.81, all-cause mortality RR 0.83; reductions up to 210-225 g/day.

pmid:30638909.authors: Reynolds A, Mann J, Cummings J, et al.
pmid:30638909.title: Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
pmid:30638909.finding: Highest vs lowest fiber intake: 15-30% lower mortality and cardiometabolic disease; greatest benefit at 25-29 g/day.

pmid:21045839.authors: Pérez-Jiménez J, Neveu V, Vos F, et al.
pmid:21045839.title: Identification of the 100 richest dietary sources of polyphenols: an application of the Phenol-Explorer database.
pmid:21045839.finding: Total polyphenols by chromatography ranged from 15,000 mg/100 g (cloves) down; Folin values systematically exceed chromatography totals.

pmid:24103452.authors: Rothwell JA, Perez-Jimenez J, Neveu V, et al.
pmid:24103452.title: Phenol-Explorer 3.0: a major update of the Phenol-Explorer database to incorporate data on the effects of food processing on polyphenol content.
pmid:24103452.finding: Describes the Phenol-Explorer database and its retention factors for food processing.

diet:phenolexplorer.title: Phenol-Explorer database: polyphenol content of foods, food pages accessed 2026-09-30 (chromatography, Folin assay and pH-differential tables).
diet:phenolexplorer.finding: Source of per-food polyphenol values used here; 'chromatography (sum of compounds)' values were computed by summing the individual compounds listed in each food's chromatography table.

diet:usdafdc.title: FoodData Central, SR Legacy food records (e.g. FDC 168153 kiwifruit, 170108 red pepper, 170379 broccoli, 170457 tomato, 170460 tomato puree, 170393 carrot, 168462 spinach, 168421 kale, 169097 orange, 167762 strawberry), accessed 2026-09-30.
diet:usdafdc.finding: Source of vitamin C, carotenoid and lycopene contents per 100 g.

pmid:25772010.authors: van 't Erve TJ, Lih FB, Kadiiska MB, et al.
pmid:25772010.title: Reinterpreting the best biomarker of oxidative stress: The 8-iso-PGF(2α)/PGF(2α) ratio distinguishes chemical from enzymatic lipid peroxidation.
pmid:25772010.finding: 8-iso-PGF2alpha can also come from enzymatic (COX) synthesis during inflammation, so rises do not always mean more chemical oxidative stress.

pmid:23596162.authors: Siervo M, Lara J, Ogbonmwan I, et al.
pmid:23596162.title: Inorganic nitrate and beetroot juice supplementation reduces blood pressure in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:23596162.finding: Nitrate/beetroot lowered systolic BP by 4.4 mmHg, dose-dependently.

pmid:20096093.authors: Carlsen MH, Halvorsen BL, Holte K, et al.
pmid:20096093.title: The total antioxidant content of more than 3100 foods, beverages, spices, herbs and supplements used worldwide.
pmid:20096093.finding: FRAP antioxidant content varies several-thousand-fold between foods; spices and herbs are highest.

pmid:15186133.authors: Wu X, Beecher GR, Holden JM, et al.
pmid:15186133.title: Lipophilic and hydrophilic antioxidant capacities of common foods in the United States.
pmid:15186133.finding: ORAC values of >100 US foods; total phenolics (Folin) correlated only weakly with hydrophilic ORAC.

pmid:38428187.authors: Favari C, Rinaldi de Alvarenga JF, Sánchez-Martínez L, et al.
pmid:38428187.title: Factors driving the inter-individual variability in the metabolism and bioavailability of (poly)phenolic metabolites: A systematic review of human studies.
pmid:38428187.finding: Gut microbiota, genetics, age, sex and BMI drive high/low excretor gradients and producer/non-producer metabotypes (urolithins, equol) for polyphenol metabolites.

pmid:25530151.authors: Rodriguez-Mateos A, Hezel M, Aydin H, et al.
pmid:25530151.title: Interactions between cocoa flavanols and inorganic nitrate: additive effects on endothelial function at achievable dietary amounts.
pmid:25530151.finding: Cocoa flavanols and nitrate each raised FMD dose-dependently (peak at 1 h) and their effects were additive at low intake levels.

pmid:32204978.authors: Alvarenga L, Salarolli R, Cardozo LFMF, et al.
pmid:32204978.title: Impact of curcumin supplementation on expression of inflammatory transcription factors in hemodialysis patients: A pilot randomized, double-blind, controlled study.
pmid:32204978.finding: A juice containing 2.5 g turmeric three times weekly for 3 months lowered PBMC NF-kB mRNA and hs-CRP (3.8 to 2.0 mg/L) but did not change Nrf2 mRNA.

pmid:42005325.authors: Bahari H, Jazinaki MS, Asadi Z, et al.
pmid:42005325.title: Curcumin/Turmeric Supplementation on Glycemic Control in Adults With Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
pmid:42005325.finding: In prediabetes/type 2 diabetes, curcumin/turmeric lowered fasting glucose (-10.2 mg/dL), HbA1c (-0.32%) and HOMA-IR, with larger effects at >=1 g/day; heterogeneity was substantial.

pmid:29622343.authors: Bannuru RR, Osani MC, Al-Eid F, et al.
pmid:29622343.title: Efficacy of curcumin and Boswellia for knee osteoarthritis: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:29622343.finding: Curcuminoids beat placebo for knee OA pain and function and matched NSAIDs with fewer GI adverse events, but study quality was low and most trials had <100 participants.

pmid:41560742.authors: Chen J, Zhou Q, Yu W, et al.
pmid:41560742.title: A critical review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of curcumin for knee osteoarthritis.
pmid:41560742.finding: Overview of curcumin-for-knee-OA reviews: methodological quality extremely low, heavy overlap, and 37 of 48 outcomes rated extremely low-quality evidence.

pmid:28358991.authors: Cowell W, Ireland T, Vorhees D, et al.
pmid:28358991.title: Ground Turmeric as a Source of Lead Exposure in the United States.
pmid:28358991.finding: Describes US childhood lead-poisoning cases traced to spices; all 32 turmeric samples bought in Boston contained lead (0.03-99.5 ppm), half above the FDA candy limit of 0.1 ppm.

pmid:29802852.authors: Cruz-Correa M, Hylind LM, Marrero JH, et al.
pmid:29802852.title: Efficacy and Safety of Curcumin in Treatment of Intestinal Adenomas in Patients With Familial Adenomatous Polyposis.
pmid:29802852.finding: Pure curcumin 3 g/day for 12 months did not reduce the number or size of intestinal adenomas versus placebo.

pmid:21413691.authors: Cuomo J, Appendino G, Dern AS, et al.
pmid:21413691.title: Comparative absorption of a standardized curcuminoid mixture and its lecithin formulation.
pmid:21413691.finding: Phospholipid curcumin (Meriva) raised total curcuminoid absorption about 29-fold, but only phase-2 conjugates were detected and levels stayed below those needed for most anti-inflammatory targets.

pmid:36804260.authors: Dehzad MJ, Ghalandari H, Nouri M, et al.
pmid:36804260.title: Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of curcumin/turmeric supplementation in adults: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:36804260.finding: Turmeric/curcumin lowered CRP (-0.58 mg/L), TNF-a and IL-6 (-1.31 pg/mL), raised TAC (+0.21 mmol/L) and SOD, and lowered MDA (-0.33 umol/L); IL-1b unchanged.

doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1679.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS)
doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1679.title: Scientific Opinion on the re-evaluation of curcumin (E 100) as a food additive.
doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1679.finding: Set an ADI of 3 mg/kg bw/day for curcumin, from a NOAEL of 250-320 mg/kg bw/day (lower F2 body-weight gain in a reproductive toxicity study) with a 100-fold uncertainty factor; not carcinogenic or genotoxic.

pmid:33174301.title: The effect of curcumin supplementation on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:33174301.finding: Curcumin lowered creatine kinase (-48.5 IU/L) and muscle-soreness scores (WMD -0.48) after damaging exercise.

pmid:34378053.authors: Ferguson JJA, Abbott KA, Garg ML
pmid:34378053.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of oral supplementation with curcumin: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:34378053.finding: Curcumin lowered CRP (-1.55 mg/L), IL-6 (-1.69 pg/mL) and TNF-a; authors note dose, duration and formulation remain unresolved.

pmid:34665507.authors: Flory S, Sus N, Haas K, et al.
pmid:34665507.title: Increasing Post-Digestive Solubility of Curcumin Is the Most Successful Strategy to Improve its Oral Bioavailability: A Randomized Cross-Over Trial in Healthy Adults and In Vitro Bioaccessibility Experiments.
pmid:34665507.finding: Head-to-head test of 8 formulations at 207 mg curcumin: no free curcumin was detected in anyone; only micelles (57-fold) and gamma-cyclodextrin (30-fold) significantly raised conjugate AUC; piperine-type adjuvants did not.

pmid:31550596.authors: Forsyth JE, Nurunnahar S, Islam SS, et al.
pmid:31550596.title: Turmeric means "yellow" in Bengali: Lead chromate pigments added to turmeric threaten public health across Bangladesh.
pmid:31550596.finding: Lead chromate pigment (2-10% lead by weight) is added to turmeric during polishing in 7 of 9 major producing districts of Bangladesh to meet demand for bright yellow colour.

pmid:39053552.authors: Forsyth JE, Mistree D, Nash E, et al.
pmid:39053552.title: Evidence of turmeric adulteration with lead chromate across South Asia.
pmid:39053552.finding: 14% of turmeric samples from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal had detectable lead (>2 ug/g); some exceeded 1000 ug/g with 1:1 lead:chromium ratios indicating lead chromate.

pmid:15668484.authors: Garcea G, Berry DP, Jones DJ, et al.
pmid:15668484.title: Consumption of the putative chemopreventive agent curcumin by cancer patients: assessment of curcumin levels in the colorectum and their pharmacodynamic consequences.
pmid:15668484.finding: 3.6 g/day curcumin for 7 days gave colorectal tissue curcumin of ~8-13 nmol/g and lowered M1G DNA adducts in tissue: the gut wall is the one site where gram doses reach meaningful levels.

pmid:36252717.authors: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, et al.
pmid:36252717.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN].
pmid:36252717.finding: US DILIN turmeric liver-injury cases rose since 2011; typically hepatocellular after 1-4 months, one death, 3 of 7 tested products contained piperine, and 7 of 10 patients carried HLA-B*35:01.

pmid:30070343.authors: Hu S, Belcaro G, Dugall M, et al.
pmid:30070343.title: Interaction study between antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement therapy and a bioavailable formulation of curcumin (Meriva®).
pmid:30070343.n: patients on antiplatelets, anticoagulants, levothyroxine or metformin
pmid:30070343.finding: 10-15 days of Meriva did not change bleeding time on aspirin/clopidogrel/ticlopidine, INR on warfarin or dabigatran, thyroid tests or glycaemia; short, uncontrolled, sponsor-linked.

pmid:24461029.authors: Jäger R, Lowery RP, Calvanese AV, et al.
pmid:24461029.title: Comparative absorption of curcumin formulations.
pmid:24461029.finding: Relative to standard curcumin, total curcuminoid exposure was 1.3-fold higher with turmeric-oil formulation, 7.9-fold with phytosome and 45.9-fold with a hydrophilic-carrier formulation (CHC).

pmid:18815282.authors: Jiao Y, Wilkinson J 4th, Di X, et al.
pmid:18815282.title: Curcumin, a cancer chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic agent, is a biologically active iron chelator.
pmid:18815282.finding: In mice with marginal iron intake, dietary curcumin acted as an iron chelator, lowered hepcidin and caused iron-deficiency anaemia.

pmid:38945354.authors: Kavyani Z, Najafi K, Naghsh N, et al.
pmid:38945354.title: The effects of curcumin supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial function: A meta-analysis of meta-analyses.
pmid:38945354.finding: Umbrella analysis: curcumin lowered CRP (-0.87 mg/L), IL-6, TNF-a and MDA, raised SOD, GPx, catalase and FMD (+1.64%), but did not significantly change TAC.

pmid:26909743.authors: Kocher A, Bohnert L, Schiborr C, et al.
pmid:26909743.title: Highly bioavailable micellar curcuminoids accumulate in blood, are safe and do not reduce blood lipids and inflammation markers in moderately hyperlipidemic individuals.
pmid:26909743.finding: 294 mg/day micellar curcuminoids for 6 weeks reached fasting plasma ~49 nmol/L but did not change lipids, CRP or other inflammation markers versus placebo.

pmid:24672232.authors: Kuptniratsaikul V, Dajpratham P, Taechaarpornkul W, et al.
pmid:24672232.title: Efficacy and safety of Curcuma domestica extracts compared with ibuprofen in patients with knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter study.
pmid:24672232.finding: Curcuma domestica extract 1500 mg/day was non-inferior to ibuprofen 1200 mg/day over 4 weeks on WOMAC, with fewer abdominal complaints.

pmid:22300367.authors: Kusuhara H, Furuie H, Inano A, et al.
pmid:22300367.title: Pharmacokinetic interaction study of sulphasalazine in healthy subjects and the impact of curcumin as an in vivo inhibitor of BCRP.
pmid:22300367.finding: 2 g curcumin inhibited intestinal BCRP and raised sulfasalazine exposure 2.0-3.2-fold in humans.

pmid:32656820.authors: Lombardi N, Crescioli G, Maggini V, et al.
pmid:32656820.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports.
pmid:32656820.finding: Italian phytovigilance cases of acute (mostly cholestatic) hepatitis were all linked to high-bioavailability, high-dose curcumin products; positive dechallenge in most.

pmid:29943914.authors: Mahale J, Singh R, Howells LM, et al.
pmid:29943914.title: Detection of Plasma Curcuminoids from Dietary Intake of Turmeric-Containing Food in Human Volunteers.
pmid:29943914.finding: After a turmeric-containing meal at South Asian culinary levels, curcumin glucuronide peaked at ~48 nM and free curcumin was detectable (3.2 nM) in only one volunteer.

pmid:33346172.authors: Menniti-Ippolito F, Ippoliti I, Pastorelli AA, et al.
pmid:33346172.title: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) food supplements and hepatotoxicity: an integrated evaluation approach.
pmid:33346172.finding: A 2019 Italian cluster of 28 acute hepatitis reports linked to turmeric supplements; product testing looked for drugs, metals, aflatoxins, dyes and pyrrolizidine alkaloids, and regulators intervened.

pmid:38809154.authors: Musso G, Pinach S, Mariano F, et al.
pmid:38809154.title: Effect of phospholipid curcumin Meriva on liver histology and kidney disease in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:38809154.finding: Meriva 2 g/day for 72 weeks: NASH resolution in 62% vs 12% on placebo and fibrosis improvement in 50% vs 8%; single trial, needs replication.

pmid:28074653.authors: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, et al.
pmid:28074653.title: The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin.
pmid:28074653.finding: Argues curcumin is a PAINS/IMPS compound that is chemically unstable, reactive and not bioavailable; states that no double-blind placebo-controlled curcumin trial had been successful as of 2017.

pmid:16870699.authors: Ng TP, Chiam PC, Lee T, et al.
pmid:16870699.title: Curry consumption and cognitive function in the elderly.
pmid:16870699.finding: Occasional or frequent curry eaters had better MMSE scores than never/rare eaters (cross-sectional association, confounding possible).

pmid:24280069.authors: Pal A, Sung B, Bhanu Prasad BA, et al.
pmid:24280069.title: Curcumin glucuronides: assessing the proliferative activity against human cell lines.
pmid:24280069.finding: Curcumin killed cancer cell lines at 1-10 uM, but its mono- and di-glucuronides (the main circulating forms) showed no antiproliferative activity.

pmid:16767797.authors: Pattanaik S, Hota D, Prabhakar S, et al.
pmid:16767797.title: Effect of piperine on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of phenytoin in patients with epilepsy.
pmid:16767797.finding: A single 20 mg piperine dose significantly raised phenytoin AUC and Cmax at steady state.

diet:cur-pubmed-retractions.title: PubMed searches 'Aggarwal BB[au] AND retracted publication[pt]' and 'curcumin AND retracted publication[pt]', run 2026-10-01 via NCBI E-utilities.
diet:cur-pubmed-retractions.finding: Returned 27 retracted publications with BB Aggarwal as author and 162 retracted publications mentioning curcumin.

pmid:28204880.authors: Purpura M, Lowery RP, Wilson JM, et al.
pmid:28204880.title: Analysis of different innovative formulations of curcumin for improved relative oral bioavailability in human subjects.
pmid:28204880.finding: A gamma-cyclodextrin curcumin complex gave 39-fold higher total curcuminoid AUC than unformulated extract, exceeding a phytosome and a turmeric-oil formulation.

pmid:30527253.authors: Qin S, Huang L, Gong J, et al.
pmid:30527253.title: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of 4 weeks or longer suggest that curcumin may afford some protection against oxidative stress.
pmid:30527253.finding: Curcumin >=4 weeks lowered MDA (SMD -0.77) and raised SOD (SMD 1.08) with no change in RBC GPx; the MDA effect appeared at >=600 mg/day curcuminoids.

pmid:12495265.authors: Rasyid A, Rahman AR, Jaalam K, et al.
pmid:12495265.title: Effect of different curcumin dosages on human gall bladder.
pmid:12495265.finding: Curcumin 20, 40 and 80 mg contracted the gallbladder by 34%, 51% and 72% within 2 h.

pmid:23107780.authors: Ringman JM, Frautschy SA, Teng E, et al.
pmid:23107780.title: Oral curcumin for Alzheimer's disease: tolerability and efficacy in a 24-week randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study.
pmid:23107780.finding: Curcumin C3 Complex 2 or 4 g/day for 24 weeks showed no clinical or biomarker benefit; native plasma curcumin was low (7.3 ng/mL) and 3 withdrew for GI symptoms.

pmid:29192329.authors: Ryan Wolf J, Heckler CE, Guido JJ, et al.
pmid:29192329.title: Oral curcumin for radiation dermatitis: a URCC NCORP study of 686 breast cancer patients.
pmid:29192329.finding: Oral curcumin 6 g/day during radiotherapy did not reduce radiation dermatitis severity versus placebo.

pmid:24402825.authors: Schiborr C, Kocher A, Behnam D, et al.
pmid:24402825.title: The oral bioavailability of curcumin from micronized powder and liquid micelles is significantly increased in healthy humans and differs between sexes.
pmid:24402825.finding: Single 500 mg dose: micronized curcumin was 9-fold and liquid micellar curcumin 185-fold more bioavailable (AUC) than native powder; women absorbed more than men.

pmid:31972171.authors: Shin JW, Chun KS, Kim DH, et al.
pmid:31972171.title: Curcumin induces stabilization of Nrf2 protein through Keap1 cysteine modification.
pmid:31972171.finding: In mouse skin and epidermal cells, curcumin binds KEAP1 Cys151 and stabilises Nrf2 to induce HO-1; tetrahydrocurcumin, which lacks the Michael-acceptor group, does not.

pmid:29246725.authors: Small GW, Siddarth P, Li Z, et al.
pmid:29246725.title: Memory and Brain Amyloid and Tau Effects of a Bioavailable Form of Curcumin in Non-Demented Adults: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled 18-Month Trial.
pmid:29246725.finding: Theracurmin 90 mg curcumin twice daily for 18 months improved verbal and visual memory and attention versus placebo and lowered FDDNP-PET signal in amygdala/hypothalamus; very small trial.

pmid:31684927.authors: Stohs SJ, Chen CYO, Preuss HG, et al.
pmid:31684927.title: The fallacy of enzymatic hydrolysis for the determination of bioactive curcumin in plasma samples as an indication of bioavailability: a comparative study.
pmid:31684927.finding: Most curcumin PK studies hydrolyse plasma before analysis and so report total (free plus conjugated) curcumin, which overstates the bioactive free fraction.

pmid:18469248.authors: Tang M, Larson-Meyer DE, Liebman M
pmid:18469248.title: Effect of cinnamon and turmeric on urinary oxalate excretion, plasma lipids, and plasma glucose in healthy subjects.
pmid:18469248.finding: Supplemental turmeric raised urinary oxalate excretion (91% of its oxalate is soluble) and did not change glucose or lipids over 4 weeks.

pmid:17044766.authors: Tayyem RF, Heath DD, Al-Delaimy WK, et al.
pmid:17044766.title: Curcumin content of turmeric and curry powders.
pmid:17044766.finding: HPLC of 28 spice products: pure turmeric powder averaged 3.14% curcumin by weight; most curry powders contained little and variable curcumin.

pmid:17116705.authors: Tuntipopipat S, Judprasong K, Zeder C, et al.
pmid:17116705.title: Chili, but not turmeric, inhibits iron absorption in young women from an iron-fortified composite meal.
pmid:17116705.finding: 0.5 g turmeric in a meal did not inhibit iron absorption (stable isotopes), whereas chili cut it by 38%.

pmid:18559556.authors: Vareed SK, Kakarala M, Ruffin MT, et al.
pmid:18559556.title: Pharmacokinetics of curcumin conjugate metabolites in healthy human subjects.
pmid:18559556.finding: After 10 or 12 g curcumin, free curcumin was detectable in only one subject; glucuronide and sulfate conjugates were found in all (Cmax ~1.7-2.3 ug/mL).

pmid:32926799.authors: Wang Z, Jones G, Winzenberg T, et al.
pmid:32926799.title: Effectiveness of Curcuma longa Extract for the Treatment of Symptoms and Effusion-Synovitis of Knee Osteoarthritis : A Randomized Trial.
pmid:32926799.n: 70 adults with knee OA and effusion-synovitis
pmid:32926799.finding: Curcuma longa extract (2 capsules/day, 12 weeks) cut VAS knee pain by 9.1 mm versus placebo but did not change effusion-synovitis volume or cartilage; funded partly by the manufacturer.

pmid:33511486.authors: Wang Z, Singh A, Jones G, et al.
pmid:33511486.title: Efficacy and Safety of Turmeric Extracts for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
pmid:33511486.finding: Turmeric extracts reduced knee OA pain (SMD -0.82) and improved function versus placebo, similar to NSAIDs; very high heterogeneity, moderate risk of bias, less benefit with higher BMI.

pmid:25431127.authors: Alumkal JJ, Slottke R, Schwartzman J, et al.
pmid:25431127.title: A phase II study of sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extracts in men with recurrent prostate cancer.
pmid:25431127.n: 20 men with recurrent prostate cancer (single arm)
pmid:25431127.finding: 200 µmol/day sulforaphane-rich extract for up to 20 weeks did not produce >=50% PSA declines (1 of 20), but PSA doubling time lengthened from 6.1 to 9.6 months.

pmid:25851421.authors: Armah CN, Derdemezis C, Traka MH, et al.
pmid:25851421.title: Diet rich in high glucoraphanin broccoli reduces plasma LDL cholesterol: Evidence from randomised controlled trials.
pmid:25851421.finding: 400 g/week of high-glucoraphanin broccoli for 12 weeks lowered LDL cholesterol by 5-7%, more than standard broccoli (2-3%, not significant).

pmid:28615356.authors: Axelsson AS, Tubbs E, Mecham B, et al.
pmid:28615356.title: Sulforaphane reduces hepatic glucose production and improves glucose control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
pmid:28615356.finding: Broccoli sprout extract (150 µmol sulforaphane/day, 12 weeks) reduced fasting blood glucose and HbA1c in obese patients with dysregulated type 2 diabetes (not in the whole group); in cells and animals sulforaphane suppressed hepatic gluconeogenesis via NRF2.

pmid:30499426.authors: Charron CS, Vinyard BT, Ross SA, et al.
pmid:30499426.title: Absorption and metabolism of isothiocyanates formed from broccoli glucosinolates: effects of BMI and daily consumption in a randomised clinical trial.
pmid:30499426.finding: Fifteen days of daily broccoli did not uniformly change isothiocyanate absorption: it rose in leaner people (BMI <26) and fell in heavier people; GSTM1 genotype had no effect.

pmid:25968598.authors: Cipolla BG, Mandron E, Lefort JM, et al.
pmid:25968598.title: Effect of Sulforaphane in Men with Biochemical Recurrence after Radical Prostatectomy.
pmid:25968598.finding: 60 mg (~340 µmol) stabilised sulforaphane daily for 6 months missed the primary PSA-slope endpoint; PSA rose less (+0.10 vs +0.62 ng/mL) and doubling time was 86% longer than placebo.

pmid:21928849.authors: Clarke JD, Riedl K, Bella D, et al.
pmid:21928849.title: Comparison of isothiocyanate metabolite levels and histone deacetylase activity in human subjects consuming broccoli sprouts or broccoli supplement.
pmid:21928849.finding: Fresh sprouts gave higher, earlier isothiocyanate excretion than a myrosinase-free supplement with equal glucosinolate, and only sprouts lowered blood-cell HDAC activity.

pmid:33839372.authors: Dickerson F, Origoni A, Katsafanas E, et al.
pmid:33839372.title: Randomized controlled trial of an adjunctive sulforaphane nutraceutical in schizophrenia.
pmid:33839372.finding: 100 µmol/day adjunctive sulforaphane for 18 weeks had no significant effect on symptoms or cognition (as summarised by a 2025 meta-analysis).

pmid:12193649.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Holtzclaw WD, Cole RN, et al.
pmid:12193649.title: Direct evidence that sulfhydryl groups of Keap1 are the sensors regulating induction of phase 2 enzymes that protect against carcinogens and oxidants.
pmid:12193649.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:12193649.finding: Showed directly that inducers such as sulforaphane react with the most reactive of KEAP1's 25 cysteine thiols, disrupting the KEAP1-Nrf2 complex so Nrf2 can activate ARE-driven genes.

pmid:27450419.authors: Duran CG, Burbank AJ, Mills KH, et al.
pmid:27450419.title: A proof-of-concept clinical study examining the NRF2 activator sulforaphane against neutrophilic airway inflammation.
pmid:27450419.finding: Broccoli sprout homogenate did not induce antioxidant genes or protect against neutrophilic airway inflammation after ozone exposure.

pmid:39929977.authors: Dwibedi C, Axelsson AS, Abrahamsson B, et al.
pmid:39929977.title: Effect of broccoli sprout extract and baseline gut microbiota on fasting blood glucose in prediabetes: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:39929977.finding: 150 µmol/day broccoli sprout extract for 12 weeks missed its primary target (fasting glucose -0.2 mmol/L vs placebo, P=0.04); responders had gut Bacteroides genes for glucoraphanin conversion; GI side effects were more common.

pmid:27935214.authors: Fahey JW, Wade KL, Wehage SL, et al.
pmid:27935214.title: Stabilized sulforaphane for clinical use: Phytochemical delivery efficiency.
pmid:27935214.finding: Stabilised sulforaphane preparations (cyclodextrin and a commercial supplement) were as bioavailable as pure sulforaphane, peaking at about 2 h, but 6 of 10 volunteers reported mild stomach upset with one form.

pmid:31261930.authors: Fahey JW, Wade KL, Stephenson KK, et al.
pmid:31261930.title: Bioavailability of Sulforaphane Following Ingestion of Glucoraphanin-Rich Broccoli Sprout and Seed Extracts with Active Myrosinase: A Pilot Study of the Effects of Proton Pump Inhibitor Administration.
pmid:31261930.finding: With a glucoraphanin plus active-myrosinase seed/sprout extract, omeprazole (less stomach acid) and enteric coating increased conversion; greater body mass reduced conversion; cytoprotective PBMC genes rose with bioavailability.

pmid:26946249.authors: Felker P, Bunch R, Leung AM
pmid:26946249.title: Concentrations of thiocyanate and goitrin in human plasma, their precursor concentrations in brassica vegetables, and associated potential risk for hypothyroidism.
pmid:26946249.finding: Goitrin inhibits thyroid iodine uptake at 194 but not 77 µmol; collards, Brussels sprouts and some Russian kale can contain that much, while commercial broccoli and kale contain <10 µmol per 100 g.

pmid:38612798.authors: Galanty A, Grudzińska M, Paździora W, et al.
pmid:38612798.title: Do Brassica Vegetables Affect Thyroid Function?-A Comprehensive Systematic Review.
pmid:38612798.finding: Systematic review: most evidence does not support antithyroid effects of Brassica vegetables in humans, especially with adequate iodine intake.

pmid:21391649.authors: Hu C, Eggler AL, Mesecar AD, et al.
pmid:21391649.title: Modification of keap1 cysteine residues by sulforaphane.
pmid:21391649.finding: Mass spectrometry with a corrected protocol confirmed that KEAP1 cysteine 151 is among the residues most readily (and reversibly) modified by sulforaphane.

pmid:41184790.authors: Kassar O, M Mansour ME, Farag N, et al.
pmid:41184790.title: Efficacy and safety of sulforaphane in schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:41184790.finding: Sulforaphane did not improve PANSS total or positive scores; a small negative-symptom benefit at 12 weeks (MD -1.06) was not sustained; lipids improved and discontinuation was lower.

pmid:22045030.authors: Kensler TW, Ng D, Carmella SG, et al.
pmid:22045030.title: Modulation of the metabolism of airborne pollutants by glucoraphanin-rich and sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout beverages in Qidong, China.
pmid:22045030.finding: Seven days of sulforaphane-rich or glucoraphanin-rich sprout beverage raised excretion of glutathione conjugates of acrolein, crotonaldehyde and benzene by 20-50% vs baseline, with no difference between beverages.

pmid:35352732.authors: Li YZ, Yang ZY, Gong TT, et al.
pmid:35352732.title: Cruciferous vegetable consumption and multiple health outcomes: an umbrella review of 41 systematic reviews and meta-analyses of 303 observational studies.
pmid:35352732.finding: Umbrella review: cruciferous vegetable intake associated with lower risk of several cancers and all-cause mortality, but evidence was mostly weak to suggestive and observational.

pmid:32084341.authors: Liou CS, Sirk SJ, Diaz CAC, et al.
pmid:32084341.title: A Metabolic Pathway for Activation of Dietary Glucosinolates by a Human Gut Symbiont.
pmid:32084341.finding: Identified the Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron operon (BT2159-BT2156) that converts dietary glucosinolates to isothiocyanates in the gut.

pmid:31250356.authors: Lozanovski VJ, Polychronidis G, Gross W, et al.
pmid:31250356.title: Broccoli sprout supplementation in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer is difficult despite positive effects-results from the POUDER pilot study.
pmid:31250356.finding: Broccoli sprout capsules (508 µmol sulforaphane + 411 µmol glucoraphanin/day) were hard to tolerate (15 capsules, nausea, high drop-out); early survival trends favoured treatment but the pilot was underpowered.

pmid:36771424.authors: Magner M, Thorová K, Župová V, et al.
pmid:36771424.title: Sulforaphane Treatment in Children with Autism: A Prospective Randomized Double-Blind Study.
pmid:36771424.finding: 50 µmol/day sulforaphane for 36 weeks produced no significant improvement in ADOS-2, SRS-2 or ABC vs placebo.

pmid:9288764.authors: Mahéo K, Morel F, Langouët S, et al.
pmid:9288764.title: Inhibition of cytochromes P-450 and induction of glutathione S-transferases by sulforaphane in primary human and rat hepatocytes.
pmid:9288764.finding: In primary human hepatocytes, sulforaphane induced GSTA1/2 and markedly decreased CYP3A4 expression and activity, while CYP1A2 was unaffected.

pmid:41692762.authors: Mastaloudis A, Holcomb L, Fahey JW, et al.
pmid:41692762.title: Exogenous myrosinase from mustard seed increases bioavailability of sulforaphane from a glucoraphanin-rich broccoli seed extract in a randomized clinical study.
pmid:41692762.finding: Adding mustard-seed myrosinase to a glucoraphanin-rich broccoli seed extract doubled sulforaphane bioavailability (39.8% vs 18.6%); bacterial glucoraphanin-converting genes correlated with conversion.

pmid:17259330.authors: Myzak MC, Tong P, Dashwood WM, et al.
pmid:17259330.title: Sulforaphane retards the growth of human PC-3 xenografts and inhibits HDAC activity in human subjects.
pmid:17259330.finding: A single 68 g serving of broccoli sprouts inhibited histone deacetylase (HDAC) activity in blood mononuclear cells at 3 and 6 h; sulforaphane also slowed prostate cancer xenografts in mice.

pmid:19336732.authors: Navarro SL, Peterson S, Chen C, et al.
pmid:19336732.title: Cruciferous vegetable feeding alters UGT1A1 activity: diet- and genotype-dependent changes in serum bilirubin in a controlled feeding trial.
pmid:19336732.finding: Cruciferous vegetable diets lowered serum bilirubin vs a vegetable-free diet, indicating induction of the drug-conjugating enzyme UGT1A1.

pmid:25165394.authors: Navarro SL, Schwarz Y, Song X, et al.
pmid:25165394.title: Cruciferous vegetables have variable effects on biomarkers of systemic inflammation in a randomized controlled trial in healthy young adults.
pmid:25165394.finding: Double-dose crucifers (14 g/kg body weight) for 14 days lowered IL-6 by 19% vs a vegetable-free diet; no effect on CRP or TNF-alpha.

pmid:24910991.authors: Noah TL, Zhang H, Zhou H, et al.
pmid:24910991.title: Effect of broccoli sprouts on nasal response to live attenuated influenza virus in smokers: a randomized, double-blind study.
pmid:24910991.finding: Four days of broccoli sprout homogenate reduced post-vaccine nasal IL-6 and influenza virus quantity and raised NQO1 in smokers; trends in nonsmokers were not significant.

pmid:35966784.authors: Nouchi R, Hu Q, Ushida Y, et al.
pmid:35966784.title: Effects of sulforaphane intake on processing speed and negative moods in healthy older adults: Evidence from a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:35966784.finding: Analysis of the same 12-week trial: glucoraphanin improved processing speed and reduced negative mood, without changes in oxidative stress, inflammation or neural plasticity biomarkers.

pmid:40988712.authors: Saito A, Ishikawa S, Yang K, et al.
pmid:40988712.title: Sulforaphane as a potential therapeutic agent: a comprehensive analysis of clinical trials and mechanistic insights.
pmid:40988712.finding: Of 84 registered sulforaphane/broccoli-extract trials only 39 were published, raising publication-bias concerns; summarises effects by disease category.

pmid:36618707.authors: Satomi S, Takahashi S, Yoshida K, et al.
pmid:36618707.title: Effects of broccoli sprout supplements enriched in glucoraphanin on liver functions in healthy middle-aged adults with high-normal serum hepatic biomarkers: A randomized controlled trial.
pmid:36618707.finding: 60 mg (137 µmol) glucoraphanin daily for 24 weeks lowered serum ALT vs placebo without changing serum glutathione.

pmid:25313065.authors: Singh K, Connors SL, Macklin EA, et al.
pmid:25313065.title: Sulforaphane treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
pmid:25313065.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:25313065.finding: 50-150 µmol/day sulforaphane for 18 weeks improved Aberrant Behavior Checklist by 34% and Social Responsiveness Scale by 17% vs <3.3% on placebo; scores reverted after stopping.

pmid:27130714.authors: Sudini K, Diette GB, Breysse PN, et al.
pmid:27130714.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Effect of Broccoli Sprouts on Antioxidant Gene Expression and Airway Inflammation in Asthmatics.
pmid:27130714.finding: Eating 100 g broccoli sprouts daily for 3 days did not reduce exhaled NO, improve lung function or induce antioxidant genes in nasal or blood cells.

pmid:29691233.authors: Tahata S, Singh SV, Lin Y, et al.
pmid:29691233.title: Evaluation of Biodistribution of Sulforaphane after Administration of Oral Broccoli Sprout Extract in Melanoma Patients with Multiple Atypical Nevi.
pmid:29691233.finding: 50, 100 or 200 µmol/day broccoli sprout extract for 28 days was well tolerated and gave dose-dependent plasma and skin sulforaphane levels.

pmid:30982861.authors: Traka MH, Melchini A, Coode-Bate J, et al.
pmid:30982861.title: Transcriptional changes in prostate of men on active surveillance after a 12-mo glucoraphanin-rich broccoli intervention-results from the Effect of Sulforaphane on prostate CAncer PrEvention (ESCAPE) randomized controlled trial.
pmid:30982861.finding: One 300 mL portion per week of high-glucoraphanin broccoli soup for 12 months attenuated cancer-associated gene expression changes in prostate tissue in a dose-dependent way.

pmid:38089924.authors: van Steenwijk HP, Vinken A, van Osch FHM, et al.
pmid:38089924.title: Sulforaphane as a potential modifier of calorie-induced inflammation: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
pmid:38089924.finding: 16 g broccoli sprouts before a high-calorie drink did not blunt the inflammatory response; CCL-2 rose slightly more.

pmid:40458076.authors: Wang R, Ren Z, Li Y
pmid:40458076.title: The effect of sulforaphane on autism spectrum disorder: systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:40458076.finding: Pooled ASD trials showed small improvements in total symptoms (SMD -0.27) and aberrant behaviour (SMD -0.43) with no excess adverse events; results depended on assessors and tools.

pmid:19349290.authors: Yanaka A, Fahey JW, Fukumoto A, et al.
pmid:19349290.title: Dietary sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprouts reduce colonization and attenuate gastritis in Helicobacter pylori-infected mice and humans.
pmid:19349290.finding: 70 g/day broccoli sprouts (420 µmol glucoraphanin) for 8 weeks lowered urea breath test, stool antigen and pepsinogens vs alfalfa sprouts; values returned to baseline 2 months after stopping.

pmid:11750273.authors: Ye L, Dinkova-Kostova AT, Wade KL, et al.
pmid:11750273.title: Quantitative determination of dithiocarbamates in human plasma, serum, erythrocytes and urine: pharmacokinetics of broccoli sprout isothiocyanates in humans.
pmid:11750273.finding: After ~200 µmol broccoli sprout isothiocyanates, plasma levels peaked at 0.9-2.3 µM at 1 h and fell with a half-life of 1.77 h; 58% of the dose was excreted in urine within 8 h.

pmid:21593509.authors: Zhang X, Shu XO, Xiang YB, et al.
pmid:21593509.title: Cruciferous vegetable consumption is associated with a reduced risk of total and cardiovascular disease mortality.
pmid:21593509.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of cruciferous vegetable intake was associated with 22% lower total mortality (HR 0.78), mainly cardiovascular, in the Shanghai cohorts.

pmid:21249160.authors: Ali MA, Poortvliet E, Strömberg R, et al.
pmid:21249160.title: Polyamines: total daily intake in adolescents compared to the intake estimated from the Swedish Nutrition Recommendations Objectified (SNO).
pmid:21249160.finding: Swedish adolescents ate ~316 umol/day of total polyamines (fruit supplied almost half); a diet meeting national guidelines would supply ~541 umol/day.

pmid:41683255.authors: Alipour M, Saeidi A, Hejazi K, et al.
pmid:41683255.title: The Effects of Interval Resistance-Aerobic Training and Fisetin Supplementation on Asprosin and Selected Adipokines in Obese Men: A Double-Blind Randomized Control Trial.
pmid:41683255.finding: 200 mg/day fisetin for 12 weeks, alone or with training, lowered asprosin and MCP-1 and improved lipids; a small single-centre trial using continuous, not senolytic, dosing.

pmid:28505227.authors: Alway SE, McCrory JL, Kearcher K, et al.
pmid:28505227.title: Resveratrol Enhances Exercise-Induced Cellular and Functional Adaptations of Skeletal Muscle in Older Men and Women.
pmid:28505227.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
pmid:28505227.finding: 500 mg/day resveratrol with 12 weeks of exercise improved mitochondrial density, fatigue resistance, knee-extensor torque (8-14%) and fibre area more than exercise alone, with no extra cardiovascular benefit.

pmid:29127724.authors: Andres S, Pevny S, Ziegenhagen R, et al.
pmid:29127724.title: Safety Aspects of the Use of Quercetin as a Dietary Supplement.
pmid:29127724.finding: Quercetin supplements up to 1000 mg/day have few reported adverse effects, but long-term (>12 week) safety data at high doses are lacking and drug interactions and kidney concerns exist.

pmid:32694802.authors: Andreux PA, Blanco-Bose W, Ryu D, et al.
pmid:32694802.title: The mitophagy activator urolithin A is safe and induces a molecular signature of improved mitochondrial and cellular health in humans.
pmid:32694802.finding: Urolithin A up to 1000 mg/day for 4 weeks was safe and bioavailable, lowered plasma acylcarnitines and induced mitochondrial gene expression in muscle.

pmid:27276742.authors: Anthanont P, Lumlerdkij N, Akarasereenont P, et al.
pmid:27276742.title: Moringa Oleifera Leaf Increases Insulin Secretion after Single Dose Administration: A Preliminary Study in Healthy Subjects.
pmid:27276742.finding: A single 4 g dose of moringa leaf powder raised insulin secretion by 74% without changing plasma glucose.

pmid:10958819.authors: Arai Y, Watanabe S, Kimira M, et al.
pmid:10958819.title: Dietary intakes of flavonols, flavones and isoflavones by Japanese women and the inverse correlation between quercetin intake and plasma LDL cholesterol concentration.
pmid:10958819.finding: Total dietary flavonol plus flavone intake averaged 16.7 mg/day (mostly from onions); quercetin intake correlated inversely with LDL cholesterol.

pmid:33801767.authors: Baynham R, Veldhuijzen van Zanten JJCS, Johns PW, et al.
pmid:33801767.title: Cocoa Flavanols Improve Vascular Responses to Acute Mental Stress in Young Healthy Adults.
pmid:33801767.finding: A cocoa drink with 150 mg epicatechin taken 1.5 h before mental stress prevented the stress-induced fall in flow-mediated dilation.

pmid:16136122.authors: Beauchamp GK, Keast RS, Morel D, et al.
pmid:16136122.title: Phytochemistry: ibuprofen-like activity in extra-virgin olive oil.
pmid:16136122.finding: Oleocanthal in freshly pressed extra-virgin olive oil inhibits the same cyclooxygenase enzymes as ibuprofen and causes the oil's throat sting.

pmid:10926790.authors: Bell MC, Crowley-Nowick P, Bradlow HL, et al.
pmid:10926790.title: Placebo-controlled trial of indole-3-carbinol in the treatment of CIN.
pmid:10926790.finding: 200 or 400 mg/day indole-3-carbinol for 12 weeks produced complete regression in 8 of 17 treated women vs 0 of 10 on placebo.

pmid:7827590.authors: Bradlow HL, Michnovicz JJ, Halper M, et al.
pmid:7827590.title: Long-term responses of women to indole-3-carbinol or a high fiber diet.
pmid:7827590.finding: 400 mg/day indole-3-carbinol for 3 months raised the urinary 2-hydroxyestrone:estriol ratio in a sustained way; 3 of 20 women did not respond.

pmid:21385509.authors: Brasnyó P, Molnár GA, Mohás M, et al.
pmid:21385509.title: Resveratrol improves insulin sensitivity, reduces oxidative stress and activates the Akt pathway in type 2 diabetic patients.
pmid:21385509.finding: 10 mg/day resveratrol for 4 weeks reduced HOMA-IR and urinary ortho-tyrosine, an oxidative-stress marker.

pmid:37252983.authors: Brickman AM, Yeung LK, Alschuler DM, et al.
pmid:37252983.title: Dietary flavanols restore hippocampal-dependent memory in older adults with lower diet quality and lower habitual flavanol consumption.
pmid:37252983.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:37252983.finding: 500 mg/day cocoa flavanols did not improve memory overall at 1 year (primary endpoint) but did in people with the lowest habitual flavanol intake or diet quality (COSMOS-Web).

pmid:36066009.authors: Cheatham CL, Canipe LG 3rd, Millsap G, et al.
pmid:36066009.title: Six-month intervention with wild blueberries improved speed of processing in mild cognitive decline: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial.
pmid:36066009.n: 86 older adults with mild cognitive decline
pmid:36066009.finding: Daily wild blueberry powder for 6 months improved processing speed vs placebo.

pmid:12960117.authors: Chow HH, Cai Y, Hakim IA, et al.
